clue.text: Nobody's right-hand man in sport.

parts.note: a sportsman who is nobody's right-hand man is one who leads with the left: a left-handed boxer or pitcher

explanation.surface: A sportsman who refuses to be anyone's loyal deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: A left-handed boxer or baseball pitcher is called this in sporting slang, so he is literally not a right-hand man.

clue.text: One has a liking for this quiet place

definitions.text: One has a liking for this

parts.note: soft means quiet, as in soft music
a spot is a place

explanation.surface: Someone is fond of a peaceful corner.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a fondness or weakness for someone is to have this.

clue.text: Showing no evidence of the cartographer's work

definitions.text: Showing no evidence of the cartographer's work

parts.words: Showing no evidence of the cartographer's work
parts.note: land with no evidence of a mapmaker's work has never been put on a map

explanation.surface: A land that no mapmaker has yet visited.
explanation.definitionFit: Territory never surveyed and never put onto maps or sea charts is unexplored.

clue.text: Hired workers get cuts

definitions.meaning: drudges hired to do routine work, especially writing

explanation.surface: Contract staff face pay reductions.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is drudge writers for hire; the other is rough chops with a blade.

clue.text: Annoyed, confused by a pain-reliever

indicators.note: confused signals that the letters of the first word are jumbled

explanation.surface: An irritated patient, muddled by a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges ANNOYED; the held '2' is the page's 'a' misread.
explanation.definitionFit: This word describes a medicine that soothes or deadens pain, and by extension anything bland.

clue.text: Garage-apprentice takes to the bottle!

parts.note: a young lad working in a motor garage could be called a ..., and the phrase is also the name of a large bottle

explanation.surface: A young mechanic's trainee turns to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as CAR BOY, the words describe a garage apprentice; as one word, it is a large glass bottle in a protective frame, used for acids or wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A carboy is a big glass or plastic flask, usually cased in a basket or crate, used to hold liquids.

clue.text: A sign of greatness ?

parts.note: a signature that a great person writes for admirers

explanation.surface: A clue that someone is truly great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' looks like an indication, but it is a signed name: famous people are asked for theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity's handwritten signature, collected by fans.

clue.text: Went the rounds — just in case?

definitions.meaning: fought a contest of several rounds in the ring
packed inside a box or case

explanation.surface: Someone did their rounds as a precaution.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is fought in the ring; the other is packed in a container.

clue.text: An agreeable fellow

parts.note: agreeable read literally: a man who always agrees with his superiors

explanation.surface: A pleasant, easy-going man.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant who always says yes to the boss is literally always agreeing.

clue.text: Demons of the loughs

annotationWithheld.why: Demons of the loughs - the wordplay is an anagram of LOUGHS, but no clue word signals the anagram ('of the' is a link), and the scan prints the clue the same way

clue.text: Confront the clergy with this aid to cleanliness

parts.note: to confront someone is to face them
the cloth is a traditional collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: Someone tackles the priesthood armed with a washing aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A small square of towelling used to wash the face is a washing aid.

clue.text: They carry a duty of one shilling

parts.note: a duty is a tax levied on goods
I is the Roman numeral one
S was the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin, from Latin solidus

explanation.surface: Goods bearing a levy of one shilling each.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-1971 British coin worth twelve pence, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabs carry passengers for a fare, so they are vehicles that carry people.

clue.text: Photos of the rest on board ?

definitions.text: Photos of the rest on board ?

parts.words: Photos of the rest on board ?
parts.note: quick pictures are ..., and the clue hints at naps taken on a ship, the S of steamship wrapped round a word for rests

explanation.surface: Holiday pictures of passengers dozing on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual photographs are informally called snapshots, shortened in everyday speech.

clue.text: To teach the blank how to shoot (Thomson)

definitions.text: To teach the blank how to shoot (Thomson)

parts.words: To teach the blank how to shoot (Thomson)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from James Thomson's poem The Seasons, about educating children

explanation.surface: A line of eighteenth-century verse with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Thomson's Spring: 'Delightful task! to rear the tender thought, / To teach the young idea how to shoot'. The blank on the page is shown here as 'blank'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the poem the phrase means a child's developing mind, which the teacher helps to grow like a shoot.

clue.text: Eight times a top clue !

annotationWithheld.why: Eight times a top clue ! - the wordplay is an anagram of TOP CLUE, but no clue word signals the anagram, and the scan prints the clue the same way

clue.text: Plant which does not give full value for money?

definitions.text: Plant which does not give full value for money?

parts.words: Plant which does not give full value for money?
parts.note: the plant's name looks like a penny's worth with its last letter missing, so it falls short of full value

explanation.surface: A factory that shortchanges its customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory. The plant's name is one letter short of PENNYWORTH, a penny's worth, so it does not give full value.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-growing plant with round leaves like coins, found on walls and in marshes.

clue.text: Hush! Poor baby's worn out!

parts.note: sh is the sound made to hush someone

indicators.note: poor signals that the letters of the following word are in bad shape and rearranged

parts.note: the word baby, its possessive ending giving no letter

explanation.surface: A parent quietens an exhausted infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' signals the anagram; read as an adjective it pities the baby, which is the misdirection. 'Hush' is the noise made to quieten someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that are threadbare and shabby look worn out from long use.

clue.text: Chaff for slimming without hesitation

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the slimming word goes round the hesitation

parts.note: banting is an old term for dieting, from William Banting's low-carbohydrate diet
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Light teasing about dieting, delivered without faltering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside'. Banting was a Victorian undertaker whose diet pamphlet made his name a word for slimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff as a verb means to tease good-humouredly, which is joking repartee.

clue.text: Wanting assistance in the home ?

parts.note: a household without domestic help, a cleaner or servant, is lacking its help

explanation.surface: A household short of a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'help' is the domestic help, a cleaner; a home without one is 'help-less'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable to manage alone, needing aid, which literally lacks assistance.

clue.text: Handsome fellow, but without trouble turns to sin

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble, as in much ado about nothing

indicators.note: turns to signals that the word sin is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the word sin, taken as written before it is turned round

explanation.surface: A good-looking man who, freed of his troubles, takes to wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns to' signals the reversal. The surface says that once the trouble is removed, what is left of the answer turns back into sin, which is how the setter hides the mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this youth was loved by Aphrodite for his beauty, so his name now means any very handsome young man.

clue.text: They give a lift to newspapermen

definitions.text: They give a lift to newspapermen

parts.words: They give a lift to newspapermen
parts.note: exclusive stories lift a reporter's career, and the same word names ladles that lift things

explanation.surface: Drivers offering rides to journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give a lift' suggests a car ride; it is the boost an exclusive story gives a journalist, and also what a ladle does.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclusive news stories that beat rival papers, and also ladles that lift out material.

clue.text: Henna mixed by a civil engineer to increase the value

indicators.note: mixed signals that the letters of the dye word are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A builder stirs up hair dye to improve its worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' signals the anagram, and suits the surface because henna is a dye mixed into a paste. The definition is 'increase the value', with 'to' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve something or raise its worth is to heighten or boost it.

clue.text: A stoppage occurs when the amber changes to green!

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of the traffic-light colour are reordered

parts.note: a green traffic light means go

explanation.surface: Traffic halts when the lights switch from amber to green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' signals the anagram. The traffic-light picture is a decoy: a green light does not stop traffic, it means go.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on trade with a country is a halt or stoppage of commerce.

clue.text: That last drink might get one caught!

definitions.meaning: a drink taken after another, such as a beer after a spirit

explanation.surface: One final drink could land a drinker in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a drink that follows another; the other is a pursuer who may catch you.

clue.text: Cells for busybodies

parts.note: busybodies suggests nosy people, but read as busy bodies it means the bees, whose wax cells hold their stores

explanation.surface: Prison accommodation for meddlers.
explanation.walkthrough: Cells look like prison cells and busybodies like nosy neighbours; the 'busy bodies' are bees, famously busy.
explanation.definitionFit: The wax structure of six-sided cells that bees build to store food and rear young.

clue.text: Government officers make good start with a loan

indicators.note: make signals that the letters are put together into a new form
start means the opening letter of good is taken

explanation.surface: Civil servants get off to a strong beginning with borrowed money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' gives G, and 'make' rearranges G and LOAN. NALGO was the National and Local Government Officers' Association, a British trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the trade union of British local government officers, so it stands for them collectively.

clue.text: County remedy for insomnia?

parts.note: read County as count-y, the clue describes the animals a sleepless person counts to fall asleep

explanation.surface: A rural shire's cure for sleeplessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County' suggests a shire, but split it as 'count-y': the traditional cure for sleeplessness is to count these animals jumping a fence. The stray 7 in the held clue is not on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting woolly farm animals leaping a gate is the proverbial way to fall asleep.

clue.text: Undercover passage in a previously peaceful neighbourhood

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is found inside the next words of the clue

explanation.surface: A secret tunnel in a once-quiet district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into 'previousLY PEaceful'. Undercover here means roofed, not secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A slype is a covered walkway, typically between a cathedral transept and the chapter house.

clue.text: Foreign coin indicated a lack of sales ?

definitions.text: Foreign coin indicated a lack of sales ?

parts.words: Foreign coin indicated a lack of sales ?
parts.note: split in two, the coin's name reads as sold followed by a nought, a record of no sales at all

explanation.surface: A coin in a dealer's window signals that business is slow.
explanation.walkthrough: The coin is an old Italian copper; read as SOLD O, it is a sales tally of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an old Italian coin of small value, one twentieth of a lira.

clue.text: Inflicted on telephone subscribers as a matter of policy?

definitions.meaning: a shared telephone connection used by several households, a nuisance for those on it
the official stance of a political organisation that its members must follow

explanation.surface: A grievance imposed on phone customers by official decision.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a shared phone circuit used by several homes; the other is a political organisation's official policy.

clue.text: Finds one's perch

parts.note: said of a bird settling for the night on a branch or bar

explanation.surface: Someone settles into their proper place.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds settle on a perch to sleep, which is the verb's everyday sense.

clue.text: Diamonds for a sucker ?

definitions.meaning: diamond shapes, rhombuses, as in heraldry
a sweet or medicated tablet that is sucked slowly

explanation.surface: Gems handed to a gullible victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sucker' suggests a dupe, but here it is something one sucks: a throat tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a rhombus shape and also a throat sweet, often diamond-shaped.
